ai_show_review.summary: Scorching Dark Star > Spanish Jam > Turn On Your Lovelight with Allman guests
ai_show_review.blurb: The show bursts from a fiery Dark Star into a seamless Spanish Jam and soaring Turn On Your Lovelight, highlighted by guest guitar work from Duane Allman and Peter Green. Pigpen’s vocal trade with Gregg Allman adds extra sparkle, while the band stays tight and high‑energy throughout.
ai_show_review.review:
February 11, 1970 at the Fillmore East delivered one of the most electrifying late‑show outings in Dead history. From the opening Dark Star, the group launched into an unbroken wave of improvisation that carried straight into a scorching Spanish Jam before erupting into a soaring Turn On Your Lovelight. The presence of the Allman Brothers and Peter Green turned the jam into a three‑guitar duel—Duane’s slide on Dark Star, Green’s liquid phrasing in the Spanish Jam, and Jerry’s tone‑bent single‑coil work feeding off each other with wild abandon. Pigpen’s organ swells and his vocal trade with Gregg Allman on Lovelight added a soulful punch that fans still rave about.

Multiple soundboard captures of this night are crystal‑clear, but the greenberg‑evans recording stands out as the cleanest, preserving every nuance of the guest contributions without any drop‑outs. The energy never wanes; even the late‑set encore “Uncle John’s Band” feels like a triumphant coda to an already legendary performance. For anyone craving a taste of the Dead at their most adventurous with top‑flight guests, this show is essential listening.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source, crisp and balanced mix that captures the guest jams and vocal trade without any drop‑outs.

key_highlights: Dark Star > Spanish Jam > Turn On Your Lovelight sequence with Allman Brothers and Peter Green.
Gregg Allman's surprise vocal on Lovelight and Pigpen’s organ burst add unique texture.
High‑energy Spanish Jam showcases multiple guest guitarists in a thrilling duel.
Soundboard recordings are crystal‑clear; the greenberg‑evans capture is the cleanest.

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers blazing guitar work, dueling with Duane Allman and Peter Green, and trades vocals with Gregg Allman on Lovelight; tone praised for single‑coil experimentation.
band_performance.Phil: Provides solid, supportive bass throughout; steps back during Lovelight to soak in the guest jam atmosphere.
band_performance.Pigpen: Adds vibrant organ swells and shares vocal duties on Lovelight, enhancing the song’s soulful climax.
band_performance.Mickey: Joins forces with multiple drummers—including Butch—and unleashes a massive gong that drives the high‑energy jams.
